description:
FILED s462at (agent AT, round 19) as the measured residue of #939 and #934 --
TWO gaps that turn out to be the SAME question asked in two families, so they
are one task: `perl refuses an operation on an overloaded object', and `substr
takes its target argument in loose lvalue context'.  Both were probed 5.40.3
vs ./runpcl on the s462at tree, AFTER #939 and #934 shipped.

=== HALF (a): the BINARY overload family still numifies where perl refuses ===

#934 shipped the refusal for `++`/`--` only, because perl's message for those
is a ONE-LINE shape of its own and the family is bounded.  The BINARY family
has a different, three-line message and a much wider blast radius, so it was
deliberately left:

    package C; use overload '0+'=>sub{5}, '""'=>sub{"S"};   # NO fallback
    my $x = C->new;
    my $z = $x + 2;    perl: Operation "+": no method found,
                             \tleft argument in overloaded package C,
                             \tright argument has no overloaded magic
                       PCL:  7
    $x += 2;           perl: Operation "+=": ... (same three-line shape)
                       PCL:  no error

The RULE is the one %p-overload-fallback-of already answers (it is written and
now read): a handler wins; else autogeneration where perl has a derivation;
else `fallback => 1' means use the ordinary semantics and anything else DIES.
The site is `p-+' / `p--' / the whole p-OP family, reached from
%p-compound-+-slow as well, so ONE placement covers `+', `+=' and the raw
`$s += $obj' twin.

WHY IT WAS HELD: DECIDED s461f's ruled caution -- a new death in a
`fallback => 1'-heavy world needs evidence.  The s462at exposure scan over
cpan-tests/ + lib/ + perl-tests/ found 23 files that say `use overload' at all:
5 with `fallback => 1', 1 with another fallback value, 17 with NONE.  That is
the population to measure the death against, plus the op/ and uni/ companion
legs, before flipping.  Note the three-line message means the two halves cannot
share a formatter.

=== HALF (b): substr's TARGET ARGUMENT is a place for `=' and 4-arg too ===

#939 made the `=~' TARGET bind the write-through cell, and it maps substr's
own first argument as well (perl's loose lvalue context), so
`substr($#ta,0,2) =~ s/\A..\z/23/s' resizes @ta.  The `=' and 4-arg spellings
of the same write do NOT, because they never pass through that routing:

    our @ta; $#ta = -1;
    substr($#ta,0,2) = 23;        perl 23   PCL -1     t/op/substr.t:889
    substr($#ta,0,2,23);          perl 23   PCL -1     t/op/substr.t:894  <- a
                                                        BLESSED SWEEP FAIL, and
                                                        it is fail 353 of
                                                        substr.t today
    my @a=("hello"); substr($a[0],0,2) = "AB";   perl ABllo  PCL hello  SILENT
    my %h=(k=>"hello"); substr($h{k},0,2) = "AB";perl ABllo  PCL hello  SILENT
    my $r=["hello"];  substr($r->[0],0,2)="AB";  perl ABllo  PCL hello  SILENT
    my @a=("hello"); substr($a[0],0,2,"AB");     perl ABllo  PCL hello  SILENT
    my $s="hello";   substr($s,0,2) = "AB";      BOTH ABllo  (works: $s IS a box)
    my $r=\my $s; substr($$r,0,2) = "AB";        BOTH ABllo  (deref gives a box)

The ELEMENT rows are SILENT WRONGS -- perl writes, PCL writes nothing and says
nothing -- and they are the bigger half by frequency.  The cause is one line:
p-substr's 4-arg form ends in `(when (p-box-p str) (box-set str new-str))', and
`(p-aref @a 0)` is a RAW element under the s455 boxed-aggregates model, so the
write silently lands nowhere.

THE FIX SHAPE, and the two pieces already exist:
  * Pl/ExprToCL.pm's `_write_through_form' (added by #939) already maps a form
    to its place twin -- element heads to their `-box' twin, magic-lvalue heads
    to their `-lvalue-cell'.  The `=' path needs substr's FIRST ARGUMENT run
    through it when the call is an assignment TARGET, and the 4-arg call needs
    the same when it has four arguments.
  * DO NOT impose lvalue context on substr's argument unconditionally: a READ
    (`my $x = substr($a[0],0,2)') would then promote the element to a box on
    every access, which is exactly the cost the boxed-aggregates work removed.
    The gate is the WRITE position, and the three write positions are
    p-setf's `p-substr' place arm, a 4-argument call, and #939's `=~' target.
  * RULE 12 belt: p-substr's 4-arg form should DIE (%p-require-writable-target,
    added by #939 for the cells) when its target is not a box, so a missed
    position is loud instead of silent.  Probe first -- it may already be
    reached by shapes perl accepts.

BAR: the eight rows above vs perl; t/op/substr.t's blessed sweep fail 353
(`substr($#ta,0,2,23)`) leaves fail-baseline BY EDIT with its cause; the #939
guard rows in Pl/t/lvalue-ref-01.t unmoved; full sweep (a `cl/' change) plus
corpus-diff for the emission half.

NOT IN SCOPE either half: `sub :lvalue'.  t/op/substr.t's remaining four rows
in that block (`ta_tindex() = 23', `substr(ta_tindex(),0,2) = 23', ...) need
lvalue subroutines, which PCL drops loudly ("PCL: Can't modify non-lvalue
subroutine call in assignment") and which is a feature of its own.

=== s463au (agent AU, round 20): HALF (b) SHIPPED.  HALF (a) SIZED AND
=== DECLINED, with the three prerequisites it needs measured and filed as #972.
=== The task stays OPEN for half (a).

--- HALF (b) SHIPPED ---

ONE REWRITER, THREE CALLERS.  `Pl::ExprToCL::_lvalue_target_form` gives a
magic-lvalue call's FIRST argument its write-through place â perl's loose
lvalue context â and is factored OUT of #939's `_write_through_form`, which
now calls it.  The three write spellings of a substr/vec/pos window
(`= V`, the 4-argument call, `=~ s///`) therefore ask ONE question.  The head
is NOT swapped for the first two: p-setf's own arms already turn
`(p-substr X S L)` into the 4-arg write, `(p-vec X O B)` into p-vec-set and
`(p-pos X)` into the 2-arg setter; what they lacked was a PLACE.

THE GATE IS THE WRITE POSITION.  A 2- or 3-argument substr READS, and
imposing lvalue context on a read would promote the element to a box on every
access â the cost the boxed-aggregates work removed.  So the `=` path keys on
the OPERATOR and the call path on the ARGUMENT COUNT (4).

`pos` GAINED ITS OTHER TWO ELEMENT KINDS.  gen_funcall's `pos` arm listed
`a_acc`/`h_acc` only; *p-match-pos* is keyed by BOX IDENTITY, so
`pos($c->{tmp}) = 0` (Text::CSV_PP's shape) wrote to a value and read undef
while the named-hash spelling worked.  A table now, like the `delete` arm
three lines below it, which has had all four kinds all along.

THE RULE-12 DEATH THIS TASK ASKED FOR IS NOT SHIPPED, AND THE PROBE THE TASK
ASKED FOR FIRST IS EXACTLY WHY.  `sub f { "hello" } substr(f(),0,2,"AB")` is
NOT an error in perl: the 4-argument form takes its target in LOOSE lvalue
context, so a TEMPORARY is written and discarded and the call answers "he".
Only the `=` spelling refuses a non-lvalue sub call, and only a READ-ONLY
literal refuses both.  A raw CL string is exactly that temporary and PCL
cannot tell it from a literal, so `%p-require-writable-target` there would
refuse a shape perl accepts.  The s329 boundary agrees: perl discards this
write itself, so no value the program consumes is lost.  p-substr's `when
(p-box-p str)` stays, with the measurement written into the comment.

BARS.  28-row probe battery 26 identical (6 before) + 18 more rows for the
shapes the A/B found; corpus-diff 1 of 111; emission A/B over 1145 files
(lib/ + perl-tests/ + cpan board + EVERY directory of perl's t/ + SHAPES):
SAME=1139 DIFF=6 RCDIFF=0, all six probed and all six the intended rewrite
(perl-tests/substr.t, t/op/substr.t, Text::CSV_PP.pm:5154, t/op/avhv.t's
`$#{$_[0]}=N` through an @_ element, t/op/tiehandle.t's buffer write,
t/op/vec.t's NESTED `vec(substr($foo,1,3),5,4)=3`); FULL SWEEP GATE clean,
TOTAL 18343 -> 18346 (+3, all substr.t), drops 5 = census; ONE pass-baseline
row edited by hand (substr.t 348/2 -> 351/0) with a serial base-tree
attribution; ONE skip registration DROPPED (test 142, found by the registry's
own `# REGISTRY-STALE` detector â it blamed tie write-through, the cause was
the raw element); guard Pl/t/lvalue-ref-01.t 31 -> 38, inverse-verified on
6e6f191; generation v2-580 + the three artifacts.

TWO RESIDUES, both measured:
  * `substr("literal",0,2,"AB")` â perl dies (read-only source), PCL answers
    "he".  PCL has no read-only scalars; the #873 family.  NOT filed
    separately.
  * `substr(X,0,2) .= "Q"` / `+=` / `vec(X,0,8) |= 65` â a COMPOUND assignment
    through the window computes the value and writes it nowhere, ON A PLAIN
    SCALAR TOO, so it is not this task's element question.  Task **#971**,
    with the mechanism (%store-back-form has no magic-lvalue arm where p-setf
    has one per head).

--- HALF (a) DECLINED THIS SESSION, AND THE EVIDENCE IS THE REASON ---

DECIDED s461f asks for evidence before a new death in a `fallback => 1`-heavy
world.  The evidence says NOT YET, for three measured reasons, all in task
**#972**:

  1. `nomethod` IS IGNORED.  perl consults it at exactly the point the refusal
     would fire, so a class that says "call me instead of dying" would be
     killed.  Probed: NoM with `nomethod => sub {"NOMETHOD"}` answers
     NOMETHOD in perl and 9 in PCL.
  2. THE BITWISE OPS HAVE NO OVERLOAD DISPATCH AT ALL, and that is where this
     half's OWN ROWS ARE.  perl-tests/bop.t 462-465 are four blessed baseline
     fails: 462/463 need the REFUSAL, 464/465 need the DISPATCH
     (`bless([],"Baz") | "x"` is 'y' in perl and '8' in PCL).  Shipping the
     refusal alone moves two of the four and leaves the other two wrong for
     the other reason.
  3. `""` IS NOT DERIVED FROM `0+`, and the refusal's own boundary depends on
     the conversion set: `.` and `x` are the two binary ops perl
     AUTOGENERATES (from `""`) and therefore never refuses.  Also the message
     names the COMPOUND operator (`Operation "+="`), which PCL's `+=` has lost
     by the time it reaches `p-+` through %p-compound-+-slow.

WHAT WAS MEASURED FOR IT, so the next session does not re-derive it (17 rows,
perl 5.40.3):
  MESSAGE SHAPE, exactly â
      Operation "OP": no method found,
      \tleft argument <in overloaded package CLS | has no overloaded magic>,
      \tright argument <same> at FILE line N.
  DIES with `0+`+`""` and no fallback: + - * / % ** & | ^ << >> <=> cmp atan2
  (and the one-argument shape for abs/neg/++/--, which #934 ships).
  DOES NOT DIE: `.` and `x`.
  `fallback => 1` never dies; `fallback => 0` forbids autogeneration too.
  SITE: `%with-binary-overload`'s fall-through (ONE macro, eight callers) plus
  `%def-overloaded-cmp`'s final else, which owns the ==/eq families and their
  `<=>`/`cmp` derivation (%with-binary-overload does NOT serve them).
  PCL's lookup is otherwise GOOD: the method-NAME handler form, @ISA
  inheritance of both handlers and `fallback`, and the `<=>`/`cmp` derivations
  all agree with perl (probed).


=== s464aw (agent AW, round 22, 2026-09-02): THE THREE PREREQUISITES (#972)
=== ARE SHIPPED.  Half (a) -- the binary refusal -- is now UNBLOCKED and is
=== all that remains of this task; half (b) shipped s463au.

What changed under it (see #972's RESULT for the measurements):
  * The BITWISE ops dispatch, so bop.t 464 (`| overload works') passes and
    only 462/463/465 -- the three that need the REFUSAL -- remain.  NOTE
    465's observed value moved 9 -> 0 (fail-baseline retagged): the Bar
    object now numifies through its `""' handler instead of its address, and
    it still needs the refusal to pass.
  * `nomethod' is consulted at exactly the point the refusal fires, so a
    class that says "call me instead of dying" is no longer killed.  This was
    the blocking objection.
  * `""' derives from `0+' (and the whole conversion matrix), so the
    refusal's boundary -- `.' and `x' are AUTOGENERATED and never refuse -- is
    now expressible: `%with-binary-overload' carries an `:autogenerated' flag
    and `p-.' is the one caller that sets it.

WHAT THE REFUSAL STILL HAS TO GET RIGHT, measured on the s464aw tree (6 probe
rows where perl dies and PCL runs):
    N0 (0+ only, no fallback)      $x + 0     perl DIES  PCL 42
    N0                             $x eq "42" perl DIES  PCL T
    N2 (0+ only, fallback => 0)    "$x"       perl DIES `Operation """"'  PCL address
    S0 ("" only, no fallback)      $x + 0     perl DIES  PCL 0
    S2 ("" only, fallback => 0)    $x + 0     perl DIES  PCL 2
    B0 (bool only, no fallback)    $x + 0     perl DIES  PCL 1
Note the THIRD row: the CONVERSION operators refuse too, with the one-line
message shape, when `fallback => 0' forbids the derivation -- so the refusal
is not only `%with-binary-overload''s fall-through and `%def-overloaded-cmp''s
final else, it is also `%p-conversion-handler''s (where #972 deliberately
returns NIL and lets the caller keep the address form, with a comment saying
the refusal owns it).

AND THE MESSAGE STILL CANNOT NAME THE COMPOUND OPERATOR (`Operation "+="'):
the spelling is thrown away by `%p-compound-+-slow' -> `p-+'.  Task #1001(b)
carries that, measured through `nomethod''s fourth argument.
subject: overload's BINARY refusal (#934's other half) and substr's target argument as a place for = and 4-arg (#939's other half)
